userJob: Decide which floor rules apply when one project holds several kinds of page
problem: A shop's about page and its order console get built against one checklist, so the console inherits marketing habits and the about page inherits console density
worksWhen: The project has more than one kind of page, or one page that both sells and operates
avoidWhen: A single page with one job, where naming the surface costs a step and changes nothing
mechanism: Name the visitor's activity on this page before layout: buying or looking at a price, operating a tool, or reading and deciding. Open only that floor. One design system spans the project, one floor governs each surface, and the direction record carries a line per surface saying what differs and why.
risks: Naming the surface after the layout is already built for a different one
Treating the surface label as a look, which reintroduces the sameness routing exists to prevent
mobileRules: Surface routing does not change at 375px; the same floor governs both widths
accessibilityRules: Every surface inherits the same floor: 4.5:1 body text, visible focus, 44px targets, 320px minimum width
genericnessNote: Routing decides which obligations apply, never what anything looks like, so two sites routed identically can still look nothing alike.

userJob: Lay out a product, listing or pricing page so a buyer can decide
problem: The object is shown on the first screen and the way to acquire it is somewhere below, so the buyer scrolls to find out whether this is even purchasable
worksWhen: Any surface where a price is visible or a transaction can start, including a single product page, a listing and a configurator
avoidWhen: An editorial page that mentions a product without offering it, where an acquire control would be a false promise
mechanism: The buyer takes in the thing and the means of acquiring it at once. On a listing the objects start on the first screen. Three shapes that satisfy it without converging: a specification whose first row is the acquire line; a full bleed photograph with the commitment spoken across it; a configurator carrying its running total from step one. Arrangement is free, co-presence is not.
risks: Reading the obligation as a hero layout and shipping the same split hero on every commerce brief
Placing an acquire control on a page where stock or price is not actually settled
mobileRules: At 375px the acquire control stays reachable from anywhere the buyer might decide, which usually means a persistent bar rather than a control only at the foot
Touch target at least 44px with 24px clearance from adjacent controls
accessibilityRules: The acquire control is a real button or link, reachable and operable by keyboard
Price and stock are readable as text, never conveyed by colour alone
genericnessNote: The obligation is shape neutral, but the first shape most builders reach for is the centred hero with a price under it, so name the shape you chose and why.

userJob: Design a console, dashboard or admin screen someone works in all day
problem: The screen is argued from dashboard conventions rather than from the work, so a dispatcher watching six things and a clerk working one record get the same layout
worksWhen: The visitor operates rather than decides: monitoring, dispatching, reconciling, editing records, running a shift
avoidWhen: A marketing page that shows a screenshot of a tool; that page is a read or buy surface, not an operate one
mechanism: Name the job's working unit first, a shift's rows or a round's stops, and fit one whole unit on screen. Measurements follow from the unit rather than from a grid you picked. Within a second the operator knows the object, its state, and the number that decides urgency. What needs deciding sorts to the top, because a screen showing everything equally has sorted nothing.
risks: Curating a subset for the operator instead of giving them filters they control
Sorting by recency because it is easy, when urgency is the axis the job actually runs on
mobileRules: If the working unit cannot fit at 375px, say which unit was split and why, rather than reflowing silently into a card list
Compared figures keep their position across widths so a column comparison does not become a stack
accessibilityRules: Every grid, scroll region and destination is reachable by key, and the key is shown on screen
A region with no focusable child passes a naive focus check and reaches nobody, so check the child, not the region
genericnessNote: Deriving measurements from a named working unit produces different layouts for different trades by construction.

userJob: Build a page whose visitor is reading or deciding, with nothing to buy or operate
problem: A reading page gets a commerce floor bolted on, so it grows a fake acquire control, a fake price anchor and trust furniture the page has no facts for
worksWhen: About pages, editorial, documentation, case narratives, campaign pages with no transaction
avoidWhen: The page carries a price or starts a transaction, which makes it a buy surface even if it reads like an essay
mechanism: There is no third floor file for reading. The core sections are the whole instruction: named subject, nouns from the subject's world, an argued direction, a planned look, and copy where every claim has a source. Strip the page to its text and read what is left; if the words alone do not persuade, the design was carrying an empty page.
risks: Inventing a floor for this surface, which produces a house style rather than a design
Adding a call to action because a page feels unfinished without one, when the page's job is to be read
mobileRules: Measure stays inside 35 to 60 characters per line at 375px
accessibilityRules: Real headings in sequence, no skipped levels
Alt text says what the image is doing there, not what it depicts in the abstract
genericnessNote: With no floor to satisfy, the reading surface is where autopilot has the least resistance, so the autopilot description matters most here.

userJob: Build a page the visitor is carried through, by scroll, animation or video
problem: Motion is added as a finish, so hover effects and reveals scatter across the page and read as machine made because nobody chose them
worksWhen: The brief asks to be carried through something, or the argument genuinely depends on sequence
avoidWhen: The page's job is to answer a question quickly; motion then sits between the visitor and the answer
mechanism: If the page moves, that is one deliberate moment and it comes from the same nouns as the signature. Everything around it holds still. Nothing moves between an intent and its result: no form animates, no click waits. Name the moment in the direction record, with the selector, before writing it.
risks: Scattering small motions so no single moment carries anything
Animating a state change that the user is waiting on, which converts polish into latency
mobileRules: Scroll driven effects respect the smaller viewport; at 375px a pinned section that needs 900px of height is a trap
Touch has no hover, so nothing that only appears on hover may carry meaning
accessibilityRules: prefers-reduced-motion stops the work, not only the visible animation
Motion never blocks input; a tap cancels an animation in progress
genericnessNote: Motion is the fastest route to a page that resembles every other animated page, because the effect library is shared and the reasons for reaching for it are not.

userJob: Improve an existing site without destroying what already works or what the client owns
problem: A redesign is treated as a new build, so brand assets, working conversion paths and hard constraints are replaced by the builder's own preferences
worksWhen: There is existing code, an existing brand, or a live page whose look must partly survive
avoidWhen: A greenfield build with no prior art, where redesign constraints would invent obligations nobody has
mechanism: Before any change, write down what must survive and why: brand marks, colour commitments, URL structure, conversion paths, content the client wrote. That list outranks general design principles and sits below only the brief's own words and factual truth. Everything not on the list is open. State the list in the report so the client can challenge it.
risks: Declaring something untouchable because changing it is hard rather than because it matters
Keeping a defect because it is old, when the defect is the reason for the redesign
mobileRules: Existing mobile behaviour is part of what must survive or be explicitly replaced; do not silently drop a working mobile pattern
accessibilityRules: Existing accessible behaviour is on the survive list by default; a redesign may not lower the floor
Never remove a protection layer without an active replacement
genericnessNote: Redesign briefs converge fastest, because the builder's fix for a dated page is the current default page.

userJob: Handle a page that both sells and operates, such as a configurator or an account page
problem: Two floors apply at once and the builder picks one, so either the commitment is illegible or the tool is decorated
worksWhen: A single page carries both a transaction and real operation, for example a quoting tool, a subscription manager, a configurator with a running total
avoidWhen: The page only looks mixed because it has a link to a tool; a link is navigation, not a second surface
mechanism: Open both floors and write one line saying which governs where. Usually the operating obligations govern the working region and the buying obligations govern the commitment region, with a stated boundary between them. Do not average the two into a third set of rules.
risks: Averaging the floors, which satisfies neither and produces a house compromise
Letting the commerce floor's emphasis rules recolour the operating region's signal colour
mobileRules: At 375px the boundary between the regions has to stay legible; stacking them without a marker reads as one region
accessibilityRules: The commitment region is announced as its own landmark so a screen reader user can reach it directly
Signal colour in the operating region keeps its meaning and is not reused for emphasis in the commerce region
genericnessNote: Naming the boundary is a decision the category does not make for you, so it tends to produce a page-specific structure.

userJob: Decide what to ship when the subject is physical and no photograph exists
problem: The missing photograph gets filled with a drawing or a generated image, so the page describes its subject instead of showing it and nobody records the gap
worksWhen: The subject is a real physical thing, place or object and no client photograph was supplied
avoidWhen: The subject cannot be photographed at all, for example a section, a schematic or a process, where a drawing is the right answer rather than a substitute
mechanism: A page about a physical subject with no photograph of it is a draft, not a failure and not a style. Name the missing asset in the asset plan, mark the build as draft so the report says so, ship it, and ask for the photograph. Never generate a picture of a place that exists.
risks: Drawing your way out of the ask, which hides the gap and reads as a finished page
Using a stock photograph of a different subject, which is a claim the client will be held to
mobileRules: A labelled placeholder reserves its aspect ratio at every width so the draft does not shift when the real photograph lands
accessibilityRules: A placeholder carries alt text naming what will occupy it, so a screen reader user is not told an image exists that says nothing
genericnessNote: Recording an absence is specific to this subject and cannot be reused, which is the opposite of a default.

userJob: Proceed when the brief does not match any known surface
problem: An unfamiliar brief either stalls the run or invents a new floor, and an invented floor becomes a house style the next brief inherits
worksWhen: The brief is a real web surface but sits outside buying, operating and reading, for example a status page, a form-only intake, an archive
avoidWhen: The brief is not a web surface at all, where the correct move is to say so and stop
mechanism: Say in the report that the brief fits none of the floors, pick the closest with a stated reason, and carry on. Do not invent a third floor. The core sections still apply in full, and the report carries the mismatch so a reader can challenge the routing rather than discovering it.
risks: Inventing an obligation set that later builds inherit as if it were proven
Choosing the closest floor silently, so the report cannot be audited
mobileRules: The chosen floor's mobile obligations apply unchanged; a mismatch in routing is not a licence to skip 320px
accessibilityRules: The floor is what varies; the accessibility floor never does
genericnessNote: An explicit mismatch note is a per-brief artefact and cannot converge.
